subject: math
cluster: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions
description: Students apply the properties of operations (commutative, associative, and distributive) to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions whose coefficients may be integers, fractions, or decimals. They combine like terms, distribute a factor across a sum or difference, factor out a common factor (including a fraction or a negative), and recognize when two linear expressions are equivalent. Answers are exact: fractions stay as fractions, never rounded decimals.
subSkills: Combine like terms within a linear expression with rational coefficients
Add and subtract two or more linear expressions, distributing a subtraction sign correctly
Expand a product by applying the distributive property, including with a fractional or negative factor
Factor a linear expression by pulling out a common factor (integer, fraction, or negative)
Apply the commutative and associative properties to rearrange and regroup terms
Determine whether two linear expressions are equivalent

problemArchetypes.name: Expand with a fractional or negative factor
Factor out a fraction or negative
Equivalence check
problemArchetypes.example: Which expression is equivalent to $6x + 9$? Answer: $3(2x + 3)$.

Easy.description: A single operation with integer coefficients. Combine like terms in a short expression, distribute one positive integer factor, or factor out a small positive integer common factor. No nested operations.
constraints: Integer coefficients only, absolute value at most $9$
One property applied (one of: combine like terms, single distribution, single factoring)
Two or three terms before simplifying
All factors and distributed values are positive integers

Medium.description: Two properties or one rational coefficient. Add or subtract two linear expressions (handling the subtraction sign), expand with a negative or fractional factor, or factor out a fraction or a negative. Up to four terms.
constraints: May include one fractional or decimal coefficient, or a negative distributed factor
Subtraction of a grouped expression that requires distributing the minus sign
Two steps such as distribute then combine like terms
Three or four terms in the working expression

Hard.description: Multi-step with two distributions and combination, fractional coefficients throughout, or factoring with a fractional or negative common factor. May require recognizing equivalence among several candidate forms.
constraints: Two distributions followed by combining like terms, e.g. $a(bx+c) \pm d(ex+f)$
All or most coefficients are fractions requiring a common denominator when combining
Factoring out a fractional or negative greatest common factor
Equivalence questions that require fully simplifying multiple expressions to compare

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student fails to distribute the negative sign across all terms when subtracting a grouped expression
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $(7x + 4) - (3x - 6)$ writes $4x - 2$ (subtracted $3x$ but kept $-6$) instead of $4x + 10$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student distributes the factor only to the first term inside the parentheses
Student combines unlike terms, adding a variable term to a constant
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Simplifies $5x + 3$ as $8x$ instead of leaving it as $5x + 3$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student factors out the common factor from only one term, leaving the other unchanged
Student multiplies the coefficients but forgets to multiply the constant term, or vice versa, when distributing a fraction
Student keeps the wrong sign when factoring out a negative
